sentences.en: After the divisiveness of the 2016 election, the Women's March became a historic symbol of unity.
sentences.zh: 在2016年大选引发的分歧之后，“女性大游行”成为了团结的历史象征。

sentences.en: Two years later, a rift has formed.
sentences.zh: 两年后，裂痕已经形成。

sentences.en: Friday, January 18th.
sentences.zh: 1月18日，星期五。

sentences.en: Farrah Stockman, how did the Women's March start?
sentences.zh: 法拉·斯托克曼，女性大游行是如何开始的？

sentences.en: So it started with an idea floated on Facebook by a woman in Hawaii who just said, we ought to have a big march against Trump.
sentences.zh: 它始于夏威夷一位女性在Facebook上提出的一个想法，她说，我们应该举行一场反对特朗普的大规模游行。

sentences.en: And it went viral.
sentences.zh: 然后这个想法迅速走红。

sentences.en: And a group of women in New York City wanted to turn that idea into a reality.
sentences.zh: 纽约市的一群女性想要把这个想法变成现实。

sentences.en: And one of the first central organizers was a white Jewish woman named Vanessa Rubel.
sentences.zh: 最初的核心组织者之一是一位名叫凡妮莎·鲁贝尔的白人犹太女性。

sentences.en: And she asked around and said, we need women of color.
sentences.zh: 她四处询问，说我们需要有色人种女性加入。

sentences.en: She asked some friends, do you know any women who would be good at helping to plan this march?
sentences.zh: 她问了一些朋友，知不知道有哪些女性擅长协助策划这次游行？

sentences.en: And she got given the name of Tamika Mallory, who was a Black gun control activist, and Carmen Perez, a criminal justice reform activiSt.
sentences.zh: 有人向她推荐了塔米卡·马洛里（一位黑人枪支管制活动家）和卡门·佩雷斯（一位刑事司法改革活动家）。

sentences.en: And they all sat down together and started planning the march.
sentences.zh: 她们坐在一起，开始筹划这场游行。

sentences.en: Well, more than 160,000 people are committed now to what's expected to be the largest demonstration in response to Donald Trump's inauguration.
sentences.zh: 目前已有超过16万人承诺参加，预计这将是针对唐纳德·特朗普就职典礼规模最大的一次示威活动。

sentences.en: Organizers of the Women's March on Washington, which is set for the day after the inauguration, they say it's unclear just how big the march is going to get.
sentences.zh: 定于就职典礼次日举行的华盛顿“女性大游行”的组织者表示，目前还不清楚游行规模到底会有多大。

sentences.en: So the march was huge.
sentences.zh: 游行的规模非常宏大。

sentences.en: In the nation's capital, hundreds of thousands turned out for the Women's March on Washington.
sentences.zh: 在首都华盛顿，成千上万的人参加了女性大游行。

sentences.en: Organizers estimate that over 4 million more rallied against the Trump administration in some 670 sister marches in cities across the country and around the world.
sentences.zh: 组织者估计，全国各地及世界各地的约670场姐妹游行中，还有超过400万人抗议特朗普政府。

sentences.en: It was way bigger than the inauguration.
sentences.zh: 这比就职典礼的规模大得多。

sentences.en: Beyond their wildest dreams, some of the organizers of the Women's March telling me here tonight they had no idea the country would respond like this.
sentences.zh: 一些女性大游行的组织者今晚在这里告诉我，这超出了她们最疯狂的想象，她们完全没想到全国会有这样的反应。

sentences.en: People came from all over, from all walks of life.
sentences.zh: 人们从四面八方赶来，来自各行各业。

sentences.en: I'm Jan, I'm from Fort Payne, and I'm here because I think we should all have equality.
sentences.zh: 我是简，来自佩恩堡，我来这里是因为我认为我们都应该享有平等。

sentences.en: We came from Durham, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我们来自北卡罗来纳州的达勒姆。

sentences.en: We took the train yesterday morning.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天早上坐火车出发。

sentences.en: We got here.
sentences.zh: 我们到了这里。

sentences.en: I am myself.
sentences.zh: 我就是我。

sentences.en: I'm a first-generation immigrant, and this really hits home very strong.
sentences.zh: 我是一名第一代移民，这对我触动非常大。

sentences.en: As a black woman with a 30-year-old black son that lives in New York City, it should be an issue for all people that our children are safe.
sentences.zh: 作为一名在纽约市抚养30岁黑人儿子的黑人女性，我们的孩子安全与否应该是所有人关心的问题。

sentences.en: We do not and we will not choose to deny our queerness, our lesbian, gay, or trans selves.
sentences.zh: 我们不选择，也绝不会选择否认我们的酷儿身份，否认我们作为女同性恋、男同性恋或跨性别者的身份。

sentences.en: They were fighting for so many causes.
sentences.zh: 她们在为许多事业而战。

sentences.en: We march to protect black colleges and black businesses, voting rights, LGBTQ rights, immigrant and disability rights.
sentences.zh: 我们游行是为了保护黑人大学和黑人企业、投票权、LGBTQ权利、移民和残疾人权利。

sentences.en: Linking this racial justice with sexism, with climate justice.
sentences.zh: 将种族正义与性别歧视、气候正义联系起来。

sentences.en: But what it does is it shows me and us and everybody here that tons of people care about the things that we care about, that we're not alone.
sentences.zh: 但这向我、向我们、向这里的每一个人表明，有无数人关心我们所关心的事情，我们并不孤单。

sentences.en: And I think it does make us feel like a more United States of America.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实让我们感觉这是一个更加“联合”的美国。

sentences.en: And it was this grand vision of where the progressive movement was going to go and how it was going to fight Trump.
sentences.zh: 这曾是一个关于进步运动走向何方以及如何对抗特朗普的宏伟愿景。

sentences.en: But behind the scenes was a different story.
sentences.zh: 但在幕后，情况却截然不同。

sentences.en: There was this growing tension, sort of a feud brewing, and that was all about power and privilege and who gets to claim the mantle of the women's rights movement.
sentences.zh: 当时存在着一种日益增长的紧张局势，一场争端正在酝酿，这完全关乎权力、特权以及谁有权主导女性权利运动。

sentences.en: So they have this amazing march.
sentences.zh: 她们举行了一场了不起的游行。

sentences.en: It's incredible success beyond their wildest dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 这是一次超乎她们最疯狂想象的巨大成功。

sentences.en: And instead of meeting to really celebrate what happened, this original group of women get together and meet.
sentences.zh: 然而，这群最初的女性并没有聚在一起真正庆祝这一成就，而是发生了争执。

sentences.en: They're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 她们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They're tired.
sentences.zh: 她们很累。

sentences.en: They're intensely irritated by one another.
sentences.zh: 她们对彼此感到极度恼火。

sentences.en: And they have essentially a fight.
sentences.zh: 她们基本上吵了一架。

sentences.en: All right, you guys, the women's march movement was supposed to bring down the president, the
sentences.zh: 好了，各位，女性大游行运动本应推翻总统，推翻

sentences.en: Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府。

sentences.en: Instead, it may not survive to the second anniversary of his inauguration.
sentences.zh: 结果，它可能撑不到他就职两周年纪念日了。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Vanessa Rubel had invited these women of color to join the leadership team.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎·鲁贝尔邀请了这些有色人种女性加入领导团队。

sentences.en: And she imagined that they would be equal partners with her and they would put on the march together.
sentences.zh: 她设想她们会成为平等的合作伙伴，共同举办这场游行。

sentences.en: But over time, she came to believe that they were taking over the march and that she was being sign-lied because she was Jewish.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，她开始认为她们正在接管游行，并且因为她是犹太人而受到排挤。

sentences.en: She says that she was told that we couldn't center the one's march on a Jewish woman because it would upset Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 她说有人告诉她，我们不能以一位犹太女性为中心来举办女性大游行，因为这会惹恼“黑人的命也是命”（Black Lives Matter）组织。

sentences.en: Some Black Lives Matter activists have made common cause with Palestinians who are living under Israeli occupation.
sentences.zh: 一些“黑人的命也是命”的活动家与生活在以色列占领下的巴勒斯坦人结成了共同阵线。

sentences.en: In fact, Linda Sarsour, Carmen Perez, and Tamika Mallory, the three women of color who joined this
sentences.zh: 事实上，琳达·萨尔苏尔、卡门·佩雷斯和塔米卡·马洛里，这三位加入团队的

sentences.en: team, all have been to Palestine and have supported the cause of Palestinian rights.
sentences.zh: 有色人种女性，都去过巴勒斯坦，并支持巴勒斯坦人的权利事业。

sentences.en: And these women have some ties to a man named Louis Farrakhan, the head of the Nation of Islam.
sentences.zh: 而且这些女性与路易斯·法拉罕（伊斯兰民族组织的领导人）有一些联系。

sentences.en: Talking about the wicked ones in the Jewish community that run America, run the government, run the world, own the banks, the means of communication.
sentences.zh: 谈论犹太社区中那些统治美国、统治政府、统治世界、拥有银行和通讯手段的邪恶之徒。

sentences.en: They are my enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们是我的敌人。

sentences.en: Tamika Mallory is close to Farrakhan.
sentences.zh: 塔米卡·马洛里与法拉罕关系密切。

sentences.en: And one of Farrakhan's big messages is that Jewish people have profited off of Black and brown bodies.
sentences.zh: 法拉罕的主要信息之一就是犹太人从黑人和棕色人种的身体上获利。

sentences.en: So this is what Vanessa says that first conversation was like.
sentences.zh: 这就是凡妮莎所说的第一次谈话的内容。

sentences.en: Tamika Mallory and Carmen Perez have a very different story of what happened that night.
sentences.zh: 塔米卡·马洛里和卡门·佩雷斯对那天晚上发生的事情有完全不同的说法。

sentences.en: And that they said, hey, we're women of color.
sentences.zh: 她们说，嘿，我们是有色人种女性。

sentences.en: We're willing to join the leadership team.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意加入领导团队。

sentences.en: But only if you let us be leaders, because we're not here as the help.
sentences.zh: 但前提是你得让我们担任领导者，因为我们不是来当助手的。

sentences.en: We're not interested in being in the background.
sentences.zh: 我们对退居幕后不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And if you want us to join with you, you got to put us in charge.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让我们加入，你就得让我们掌权。

sentences.en: And they claim that Vanessa Rubel said, well, I'm a Jewish woman.
sentences.zh: 她们声称凡妮莎·鲁贝尔说，好吧，我是犹太女性。

sentences.en: I don't have white privilege.
sentences.zh: 我没有白人特权。

sentences.en: And that their response was, yes, you do.
sentences.zh: 而她们的回应是，不，你有。

sentences.en: So Vanessa Rubel, the white Jewish woman, is claiming anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 所以，白人犹太女性凡妮莎·鲁贝尔声称遭到了反犹主义对待。

sentences.en: And the women of color are saying, no, no, no, we're not anti-Semitic.
sentences.zh: 而有色人种女性则说，不，不，不，我们不是反犹主义者。

sentences.en: But we think that people of color need to lead this march because we're not going to be secondary to anyone.
sentences.zh: 但我们认为有色人种需要领导这次游行，因为我们不会再屈居任何人之下。

sentences.en: Not anymore.
sentences.zh: 再也不会了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what ends up happening as a result of this fight?
sentences.zh: 那么这场争斗最终导致了什么结果？

sentences.en: Essentially, the women of color that Vanessa Rubel had invited initially to join end up telling her, we don't want to organize with you anymore.
sentences.zh: 本质上，凡妮莎·鲁贝尔最初邀请加入的有色人种女性最终告诉她，我们不想再和你一起组织了。

sentences.en: And they kick her out.
sentences.zh: 她们把她踢出了局。

sentences.en: And she left and she started a rival organization called March On.
sentences.zh: 她离开了，并创办了一个名为“March On”的竞争组织。

sentences.en: The other organization, Women's March, which is still led by Tamika Mallory, Linda Sarsour,
sentences.zh: 另一个组织“女性大游行”，仍然由塔米卡·马洛里、琳达·萨尔苏尔、

sentences.en: Carmen, they see themselves as claiming the mantle.
sentences.zh: 卡门领导，她们认为自己才是正统的继承者。

sentences.en: And they go on to plan their own activities, which are sometimes in conflict with what March On is doing.
sentences.zh: 她们继续策划自己的活动，这些活动有时与“March On”的行动相冲突。

sentences.en: So this thing that began as a symbol of unity for women across the country has now broken apart.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个最初作为全国女性团结象征的运动，现在已经分崩离析了。

sentences.en: Yes, it has splintered.
sentences.zh: 是的，它已经分裂了。

sentences.en: And there are now factions that are pretty openly vying against one another.
sentences.zh: 现在各派系之间正在公开地相互竞争。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the fight between these two camps of women who created the Women's March is much bigger than the grievances and the words that they exchanged.
sentences.zh: 听起来，创建“女性大游行”的这两个女性阵营之间的斗争，远比她们交换的怨言和言辞要复杂得多。

sentences.en: So what is it that's really animating this fight?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底是什么在推动这场斗争呢？

sentences.en: There has always been this tension over whether the women's rights movement was about only the needs of well-off white women or was it about the needs of all women?
sentences.zh: 关于女性权利运动究竟是只关注富裕白人女性的需求，还是关注所有女性的需求，一直存在这种紧张关系。

sentences.en: And how do you incorporate the needs of all women in your agenda?
sentences.zh: 你如何在你的议程中纳入所有女性的需求？

sentences.en: You can see this as a debate or a struggle over what are we marching for?
sentences.zh: 你可以将其视为一场关于“我们为何而游行”的辩论或斗争。

sentences.en: Which rights and whose rights?
sentences.zh: 为了哪些权利？为了谁的权利？

sentences.en: Are we marching for Black women, undocumented, gay women?
sentences.zh: 我们是为黑人女性、无证移民、女同性恋者游行吗？

sentences.en: Are we marching for Palestinian rights?
sentences.zh: 我们是为巴勒斯坦人的权利游行吗？

sentences.en: Or should we just stick to access to abortion and equal pay and trying to break the glass ceilings of corporations?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该只坚持堕胎权、同工同酬，并试图打破企业中的玻璃天花板？

sentences.en: And that question has always been there from the beginning of the history.
sentences.zh: 这个问题从历史的一开始就一直存在。

sentences.en: You can go back to the very first Women's March on Washington, which happened in 1913.
sentences.zh: 你可以追溯到1913年举行的第一次华盛顿女性大游行。

sentences.en: They were marching for the right to vote.
sentences.zh: 她们当时是为了争取投票权而游行。

sentences.en: And the 69-year drive by women for the right to vote is climaxed by this appeal at the White
sentences.zh: 女性为争取投票权进行了69年的努力，最终在白宫前达到了高潮。

sentences.en: House.
sentences.zh: （白宫）

sentences.en: And Black women were asked to march at the back of the line because they were told, hey,
sentences.zh: 当时黑人女性被要求在队伍后面游行，因为有人告诉她们，嘿，

sentences.en: if you march up at the front, it's going to offend white Southern suffragists who are there.
sentences.zh: 如果你在前面游行，会冒犯在场的南方白人妇女参政论者。

sentences.en: So Black women were included, but they were completely marginalized to the degree that they were included.
sentences.zh: 所以黑人女性被包括在内了，但她们在被纳入的程度上完全被边缘化了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So even in the 1960s, when you have the second wave feminist movement, when you look at Betty
sentences.zh: 所以即使在20世纪60年代，当你看到第二波女权主义运动，当你审视贝蒂·弗里丹和《女性的奥秘》时，

sentences.en: Friedan and the feminine mystique, it was all about suburban white women who were really bored with their lives.
sentences.zh: 那完全是关于那些对生活感到厌倦的郊区白人女性。

sentences.en: Each woman had been struggling with all these things alone.
sentences.zh: 每个女性都曾独自与所有这些事情作斗争。

sentences.en: I mean, if she was a person, if she felt there had to be more somehow than baking bread or something, she was a freak.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果她是一个人，如果她觉得生活除了烤面包之类的东西之外一定还有更多意义，她就会被视为怪胎。

sentences.en: There was something wrong with her.
sentences.zh: 她一定有什么问题。

sentences.en: But in my own suburb, it was so threatening, you know, to, I think, to the other women that I had the carpool with.
sentences.zh: 但在我自己的郊区，这太具有威胁性了，你知道，对于那些和我一起拼车的其他女性来说。

sentences.en: And I sort of became a leper, like a pariah.
sentences.zh: 我成了一个麻风病人，一个被排斥的人。

sentences.en: And it was just too threatening at first to some of these other women.
sentences.zh: 起初，这对其他一些女性来说太具威胁性了。

sentences.en: And so Betty Friedan really wanted to portray the women's rights movement as upstanding and normal.
sentences.zh: 所以贝蒂·弗里丹真的想把女性权利运动描绘成体面和正常的。

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't mean that we give up the home, but it has to be a different kind of home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不意味着我们放弃家庭，但它必须是一种不同类型的家庭。

sentences.en: We can't juSt...
sentences.zh: 我们不能只是……

sentences.en: She wanted this to be socially acceptable everywhere.
sentences.zh: 她希望这在任何地方都能被社会所接受。

sentences.en: And so she kind of whitewashed it.
sentences.zh: 所以她有点粉饰了它。

sentences.en: It was not about Black women and Latina women who had always been working, right?
sentences.zh: 这与一直都在工作的黑人女性和拉丁裔女性无关，对吧？

sentences.en: They'd always had to work.
sentences.zh: 她们一直都必须工作。

sentences.en: There were lesbians in that movement.
sentences.zh: 那场运动中也有女同性恋者。

sentences.en: She hid them in the closet and under the rug.
sentences.zh: 她把她们藏在衣柜里，藏在地毯下。

sentences.en: She didn't want anything that looked radical.
sentences.zh: 她不想让任何看起来激进的东西出现。

sentences.en: And I think that was a tactical choice on her part.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是她的一种策略选择。

sentences.en: She didn't want it to be threatening.
sentences.zh: 她不想让它具有威胁性。

sentences.en: But to a lot of women of color or to gay women at the time, they felt sidelined.
sentences.zh: 但对于当时许多有色人种女性或女同性恋者来说，她们感到被边缘化了。

sentences.en: They felt as though their voices weren't being heard.
sentences.zh: 她们觉得自己的声音没有被听到。

sentences.en: They felt left out.
sentences.zh: 她们感到被排斥在外。

sentences.en: So her view is that this is controversial enough as it is.
sentences.zh: 所以她的观点是，这本身就已经够有争议了。

sentences.en: So let's put white women who are, in her mind, the least controversial messengers at the front of it.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们把那些在她看来争议最小的白人女性作为运动的代言人放在最前面。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that the white upper class educated women were the face of that movement.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为受过教育的白人上层阶级女性是那场运动的门面。

sentences.en: And if you look at who's really benefited, who's done well since the 70s, that group of women has made huge strides.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看自70年代以来谁真正受益了，谁发展得好，那群女性确实取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: If confirmed, she will be the first woman in 191 years, indeed the first woman ever to serve on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果获得确认，她将成为191年来第一位女性，事实上也是有史以来第一位在美国最高法院任职的女性。

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: （最高法院）

sentences.en: Sandra Day O'Connor, a 51-year-old judge from the Arizona Court of Appeals.
sentences.zh: 桑德拉·戴·奥康纳，一位来自亚利桑那州上诉法院的51岁法官。

sentences.en: As the challenger climbed today, it carried an American woman astronaut, Sally Ride, into space and into history.
sentences.zh: 随着挑战者号今天升空，它将美国女宇航员萨莉·赖德送入了太空，也送入了历史。

sentences.en: A historic day in the House as Nancy Pelosi has elected the first woman speaker.
sentences.zh: 众议院历史性的一天，南希·佩洛西当选为第一位女性议长。

sentences.en: My next guest is Facebook's chief operating officer and founder of the Lean In Movement.
sentences.zh: 我的下一位嘉宾是Facebook的首席运营官和“向前一步”（Lean In）运动的创始人。

sentences.en: Please welcome Sheryl Sandberg.
sentences.zh: 请欢迎谢丽尔·桑德伯格。

sentences.en: They have broken a lot of glass ceilings.
sentences.zh: 她们打破了许多无形的玻璃天花板。

sentences.en: But if you add class into it or race into it, it's been more of a struggle.
sentences.zh: 但如果把阶级或种族因素加进去，情况就变得更加艰难了。

sentences.en: What lessons do you think that each camp that currently divides the women's movement and
sentences.zh: 你认为目前分裂妇女运动的各个阵营，

sentences.en: march, what lessons do you think that they've learned from that history that you just explained?
sentences.zh: 以及游行队伍，从你刚才解释的那段历史中学到了什么教训？

sentences.en: Well, I think the women of color who joined the leadership team said, hey, we're not just going to join.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为加入领导团队的有色人种女性说，嘿，我们不仅仅是加入而已。

sentences.en: We want to be leaders.
sentences.zh: 我们想要成为领导者。

sentences.en: We want to lead this march.
sentences.zh: 我们想要领导这场游行。

sentences.en: We are going to be front and center.
sentences.zh: 我们要站在最前线，成为焦点。

sentences.en: We're going to be unapologetically black, visibly Muslim.
sentences.zh: 我们要毫不掩饰自己的黑人身份，也要展现穆斯林身份。

sentences.en: We are going to be out there talking about these issues.
sentences.zh: 我们要走出去，讨论这些议题。

sentences.en: We're going to have trans women on stage.
sentences.zh: 我们要让跨性别女性登上舞台。

sentences.en: We're going to send every memo possible to the world that this is not your grandma's women's rights movement.
sentences.zh: 我们要向世界发出一切可能的信号，告诉大家这不再是你祖母那个时代的妇女权利运动了。

sentences.en: We're not marching so that you white women can go serve on a corporate board.
sentences.zh: 我们游行不是为了让你们这些白人女性去企业董事会任职。

sentences.en: And it sounds like their thinking is if we don't lead the movement, then we'll be left behind as we always were in past iterations of the women's.
sentences.zh: 听起来她们的想法是，如果我们不领导这场运动，那么我们就会像过去妇女运动的历次迭代中那样被抛在后面。

sentences.en: I think I think that's part of it.
sentences.zh: 我想，我想这确实是原因之一。

sentences.en: They would say that this is the first time in history that marginalized women are leading the mainstream women's rights movement and that you're going to get a better result.
sentences.zh: 她们会说，这是历史上第一次由边缘化女性领导主流妇女权利运动，而且你会得到更好的结果。

sentences.en: They would argue you're going to get more powerful coalitions because they're at the front that when black women get rights, all women will have rights because black women
sentences.zh: 她们会争辩说，你会得到更强大的联盟，因为她们站在最前线；当黑人女性获得权利时，所有女性都将获得权利，因为黑人女性

sentences.en: are the last to get rights.
sentences.zh: 是最后获得权利的群体。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they would argue that once we meet the needs of the most vulnerable, everybody else's needs will be met.
sentences.zh: 所以她们会认为，一旦我们满足了最弱势群体的需求，其他所有人的需求也就都能得到满足。

sentences.en: But the question is, who else should be included?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，还应该包括谁呢？

sentences.en: So if you're a white woman in Kentucky, you know, if you're a woman fighting for access to abortions in Texas, a white woman there, does your voice matter or are you simply a
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是肯塔基州的一名白人女性，你知道，如果你是德克萨斯州一名争取堕胎权的女性，一位那里的白人女性，你的声音还重要吗？还是说你仅仅是一个

sentences.en: person with white privilege who should listen more and take directives from this group of women in New York City?
sentences.zh: 拥有白人特权的人，应该多听少说，并接受这群纽约市女性的指令？

sentences.en: And what about the other side, the other camp that has broken off?
sentences.zh: 那么另一方，那个分裂出去的阵营又怎么说呢？

sentences.en: I think the other side would say, hey, we want you as partners and we want to be good allies, but we don't want to be sideline either.
sentences.zh: 我想另一方会说，嘿，我们希望你们成为伙伴，我们也想成为好的盟友，但我们也不想被边缘化。

sentences.en: Can't we all be leaders?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不能都是领导者吗？

sentences.en: Can't we all work together?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不能一起合作吗？

sentences.en: Why do I have to make myself small for you to have a leadership role?
sentences.zh: 为什么为了让你拥有领导角色，我就必须让自己变得渺小？

sentences.en: Can't we be all together here on the same team?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不能都在同一个团队里吗？

sentences.en: It's not that the white women who were a part of that didn't see the importance, but I think they had a hard time working their butts off and then being told, be quiet.
sentences.zh: 并不是说参与其中的白人女性不明白其重要性，但我认为她们很难接受在拼命工作之后，却被告知要保持安静。

sentences.en: This is not about you.
sentences.zh: 这与你无关。

sentences.en: In a way, this really reminds me of the battles underway in our larger politics in this country,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这确实让我想起了我们国家更广泛的政治斗争，

sentences.en: especially inside the Democratic Party, which is now debating what exactly its focus should be.
sentences.zh: 特别是在民主党内部，该党现在正在辩论其重点究竟应该是什么。

sentences.en: Should it be focused on long term liberal goals around identity and equality?
sentences.zh: 是应该专注于围绕身份和平等的长期自由主义目标吗？

sentences.en: Should that be what the party stands for?
sentences.zh: 这应该是该党的立场吗？

sentences.en: Or should it be about shorter term goals like beating the president in the next election?
sentences.zh: 还是应该关注短期目标，比如在下次选举中击败总统？

sentences.en: Because both of those goals might not be possible, which sounds like the debate you've been outlining, the kind of the question of purity versus pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 因为这两个目标可能无法兼得，这听起来就像你一直在概述的辩论，即纯粹性与实用主义的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there are a lot of echoes of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为有很多与之呼应的声音。

sentences.en: So some Democrats talk about these rural white voters.
sentences.zh: 所以一些民主党人谈论这些农村白人选民。

sentences.en: How do we get back working class whites?
sentences.zh: 我们如何争取回工人阶级白人？

sentences.en: And, you know, others say, well, you know, let them go because they are not going to vote in your interests.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，其他人说，好吧，你知道，让他们走吧，因为他们不会投出符合你们利益的票。

sentences.en: And we're tired of being sacrificed so that they can take priority.
sentences.zh: 我们厌倦了为了让他们获得优先权而做出牺牲。

sentences.en: The percentages of black women that vote loyally for the Democratic Party and 93%, 96% you see in these elections.
sentences.zh: 忠实投票给民主党的黑人女性比例高达93%到96%，你在这些选举中都能看到。

sentences.en: And then the percentages of white women that vote for the Democratic Party, in some cases it's 40%.
sentences.zh: 而白人女性投票给民主党的比例，在某些情况下只有40%。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that alone has been used.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，仅这一点就被利用了。

sentences.en: Those statistics are used by women of color who say, we're the loyal ones.
sentences.zh: 这些统计数据被有色人种女性所利用，她们说，我们才是忠诚的。

sentences.en: We're the ones who need to be put forth as the leaders because we're the ones who actually get it done and go out there and vote.
sentences.zh: 我们才是需要被推举为领导者的人，因为我们才是真正把事情做成并走出去投票的人。

sentences.en: And we're the ones you've been taking for granted all this time.
sentences.zh: 而我们正是你们一直以来视为理所当然的人。

sentences.en: In the same way they feel they've been taken for granted by the women's movement.
sentences.zh: 就像她们觉得自己在妇女运动中被视为理所当然一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, Tamika Mallory will say that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，塔米卡·马洛里（Tamika Mallory）会这么说。

sentences.en: And white women who worked in the Women's March were tired of being told over and over again that a majority of white women voted for Trump and they said, I didn't vote for
sentences.zh: 而在妇女大游行中工作的白人女性，厌倦了被一遍又一遍地告知大多数白人女性投票给了特朗普，她们说，我没有投票给

sentences.en: Trump and I'm here working my butt off with you.
sentences.zh: 特朗普，我在这里和你们一起拼命工作。

sentences.en: Why do I get this thrown in my face every day?
sentences.zh: 为什么我每天都要面对这种指责？

sentences.en: So even though people say they agree on the basic vision of where we should go as a country or on the principles, when you get down in the trenches, these are what the fights are
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管人们说他们在国家未来应该走向何方或原则问题上达成了一致，但当你深入基层时，这些就是争论的焦点。

sentences.en: about.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，究竟是谁在负责这些机构、这些政党、这些运动？

sentences.en: Which is to say, who exactly is in charge of these institutions, these parties, these movements?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 谁有权领导？

sentences.en: Who gets to lead?
sentences.zh: 谁有权成为代表人物？

sentences.en: Who gets to be the face of it?
sentences.zh: 谁的需求被优先考虑？

sentences.en: And whose needs are taken care of first?
sentences.zh: 那么法拉（Farrah），这个周末，许多美国大城市都将举行游行。

sentences.en: So Farrah, this weekend, there will be marches in many big American cities.
sentences.zh: 那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: What is that going to be like?
sentences.zh: 这个周六，我们将迎来那场游行的两周年纪念。

sentences.en: So this Saturday, we have the second anniversary of that march.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市，将会有两场游行。

sentences.en: In New York City, there's going to be two marches.
sentences.zh: 在费城，也会有两场游行。

sentences.en: In Philadelphia, there's going to be two marches.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地，都在谈论这种分裂。

sentences.en: And all across the country, there's talk of this division.
sentences.zh: 人们真的必须决定哪场游行让他们感觉更合适。

sentences.en: And people really have to decide which march feels more right for them.
sentences.zh: 有一场游行自称是由有色人种女性领导的。

sentences.en: And there's a march that bills itself as being led by women of color.
sentences.zh: 还有一场游行自称欢迎犹太女性并反对反犹太主义。

sentences.en: And there's a march that bills itself as being welcoming to Jewish women and against anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 人们将不得不决定他们想参加哪场游行。

sentences.en: People are going to have to decide which march they want to go to.
sentences.zh: 而在那个选择中，他们实际上是在表达对女权主义复杂历史的看法，以及他们认为现在谁应该领导这场运动。

sentences.en: And in that choice, they're kind of saying something meaningful about how they view that complicated history of feminism and who they think should lead the movement now.
sentences.zh: 还有一种可能性是，人们摊开双手说，好吧，我想我还是不去参加游行了。

sentences.en: And there's also the possibility that people throw up their hands and say, well, I guess I'm not going to go to a march.
sentences.zh: 这对妇女运动来说不一定是一件好事。

sentences.en: And that's not necessarily a great thing for the women's movement.
sentences.zh: 法拉，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Farrah, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 嘿，非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Hey, thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 一份新的报告估计，特朗普政府将数千名移民儿童与父母分离，其数量比之前已知的要多。

sentences.en: A new report estimates that the Trump administration separated thousands more migrant children from their parents than was previously known.
sentences.zh: 这份由卫生与公众服务部监察长进行的报告，

sentences.en: The report, conducted by the inspector general of the Department of Health and Human Services,
sentences.zh: 发现政府在2017年夏天就开始在边境分离儿童，比2018年春季宣布这一政策早了几个月。

sentences.en: found that the administration began separating children at the border in the summer of 2017, months before announcing it would in the spring of 2018.
sentences.zh: 但由于记录保存得太差，无法得知实际发生了多少起分离事件。

sentences.en: But kept such poor records that it's impossible to know how many separations actually occurred.
sentences.zh: 在众议院议长南希·佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）要求总统因政府停摆而推迟国情咨文演讲的一天后，

sentences.en: And a day after House Speaker Nancy Pelosi asked the president to postpone his State of the Union address because of the government shutdown,
sentences.zh: 总统做出了回应，取消了佩洛西原定于周四下午前往阿富汗的行程。

sentences.en: the president has responded by canceling a trip Pelosi had planned to Afghanistan, scheduled for Thursday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 白宫传统上会为这类国会行程提供军事运输。

sentences.en: The White House traditionally provides military transport for such congressional trips.
sentences.zh: 但总统表示他将拒绝提供，并称佩洛西应该留在华盛顿谈判以结束联邦政府停摆。

sentences.en: But the president said he would withhold it, in this case, arguing Pelosi should remain in Washington to negotiate the end of the federal shutdown.
sentences.zh: 在给佩洛西的一封信中，总统写道，引用如下：

sentences.en: In a letter to Pelosi, the president wrote, quote,
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你想通过乘坐商业航班进行这次旅行，那当然是你的特权。

sentences.en: Obviously, if you would like to make the journey by flying commercial, that would certainly be your prerogative.

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场痛苦、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
